entries.partTitle: Aurora Distributed Storage Architecture: 4-of-6 Quorum, Log Is The Database & Multi-AZ Striping

left.title: Monolithic Database
items: Compute and single disk volume tightly coupled.
Writes full dirty memory pages across network.
High input output latency limits transaction speed.

right.title: Aurora Distributed Tier
items: Streams lightweight redo log records to storage.
Six copies replicated across three distinct zones.
Quorum model commits with four of six confirmations.

steps.annotation: Monolithic databases suffer input output storage write bottlenecks.
Aurora decouples compute nodes from distributed storage fleets.
Engine verifies storage write quorum across healthy storage nodes.
Quorum commits survive entire availability zone infrastructure failure.

entries.partTitle: Aurora Serverless v2 Auto-Scaling Mechanics: ACU Granularity & Instant In-Place Scaling

left.title: Provisioned Compute
items: Provisioning for peak causes massive idle waste.
Provisioning for average risks overload during surges.
Resizing instances requires disruptive database restarts.

right.title: Serverless v2 Scaling
items: Scales in granular fractional capacity unit increments.
Dynamically resizes buffer pools without dropped connections.
Eliminates infrastructure cost waste during quiet periods.

steps.annotation: Static capacity sizing causes infrastructure waste or database throttling.
Serverless scaling dynamically adjusts capacity in fractional increments.
Scaler absorbs connection spikes by dynamically raising capacity units.
Granular scaling preserves active connections without downtime or restarts.

entries.partTitle: High-Performance Read Scaling: Shared Storage Replicas & Custom Endpoints

left.title: Traditional Replicas
items: Each replica maintains independent physical storage.
Streams heavy write logs causing minutes of lag.
Multiplies enterprise storage costs significantly.

right.title: Aurora Shared Storage
items: Up to fifteen replicas attach to single shared volume.
Lightweight cache invalidations keep lag under ten milliseconds.
Custom endpoints isolate analytical queries from real time traffic.

steps.annotation: Traditional replication duplicates storage and incurs severe replica lag.
Aurora read replicas attach directly to single shared storage volume.
Cluster fleet routes read requests across low latency replica nodes.
Shared storage architecture guarantees sub ten millisecond replica lag.

entries.partTitle: Aurora Global Database: Cross-Region Storage Replication & Headless Disaster Recovery

left.title: Logical Cross-Region
items: Primary compute instance handles cross region transport.
Replication lag stretches across minutes under load.
Significant risk of data loss during regional outages.

right.title: Aurora Global Database
items: Storage fleet replicates directly over private global network.
Sub second replication lag delivers near zero recovery point.
Planned failover executes role switchover with zero data loss.

steps.annotation: Traditional cross region replication degrades primary compute performance.
Aurora replicates at storage layer without consuming compute resources.
Global database coordinates planned switchover across regional clusters.
Planned role switchover completes with zero data loss recovery point.

entries.partTitle: Aurora Connection Pooling & High Availability: Amazon RDS Proxy & Fast Failover

left.title: Direct DB Connections
items: Ephemeral serverless functions exhaust connection pools.
High memory overhead per connection degrades database.
Failover requires waiting for slow client DNS propagation.

right.title: Amazon RDS Proxy
items: Multiplexes thousands of clients over compact connection pool.
Preserves client socket connections during failover events.
Reduces application observed failover downtime by sixty-six percent.

steps.annotation: Surging serverless functions exhaust relational database connection pools.
Database proxy multiplexes client sessions over persistent connection pool.
Proxy manager handles client surge without exhausting backend database.
Connection pooling preserves client sockets during failover events.
